discovery: Establishing ground-based very-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy with stereoscopic imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, revealing the Galactic population of TeV sources and cosmic-ray accelerators in supernova remnants

nominees.name: Felix Aharonian
nominees.affiliation: Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies and Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics, Heidelberg

nominees.name: Werner Hofmann
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics, Heidelberg

motivation: The origin of Galactic cosmic rays was a hundred-year-old puzzle. Aharonian and Hofmann turned it into an observational science. Hofmann led the development of the stereoscopic imaging atmospheric Cherenkov technique, culminating in H.E.S.S. Aharonian supplied the theoretical framework connecting TeV emission to particle acceleration and radiation physics, and drove its scientific exploitation. Together they produced the first resolved TeV images of supernova remnants such as RX J1713.7-3946, showing shell-type remnants accelerating particles to beyond 100 TeV. The H.E.S.S. Galactic Plane Survey uncovered dozens of new sources, including pulsar wind nebulae, binaries and dark accelerators. They also found evidence for a PeV accelerator at the Galactic Centre. This work opened a new electromagnetic window, made diffusive shock acceleration quantitatively testable, and laid the basis for CTA and LHAASO. It reshaped our understanding of how massive stars and their remnants energize galaxies.
